$comment: THE AUTHORITATIVE CI PIPELINE. Both the local Docker run (scripts/ci.ps1 | ci.sh) and the GitHub workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) execute this list via scripts/ci-stages.mjs. Neither redefines it. Adding a check here adds it to both; there is deliberately no second place to edit.

runtime.$comment: Pinned to match the version the GitHub workflow requests, so a failure that reproduces locally reproduces there. package.json declares engines.node >= 18; 20 is the tested floor.

stages.name: Source inventory
stages.why: Proves the standards series and the prohibition register have not silently changed shape. artifacts/standards-source-inventory.json was reviewed by a human and committed; this compares extraction from the source prompts against it rather than re-deriving counts. It is also protection #2 of the standards-integrity invariant: a prohibition cannot be deleted, renamed, or reclassified without failing here.

stages.name: Source fidelity
stages.why: Holds each standard to its own word: any block claiming to be verbatim from a source prompt must be verbatim, and any examples/ path a standard cites must exist.

stages.name: Policies
stages.why: Validates project-policy.yml and betting-policy.yml against their schemas. Exit 2 (malformed) and exit 1 (a compliance condition such as an expired exception) are both failures here, and both are meant to be: a policy nothing can read is worse than one that reports a problem.

stages.name: Diagram freshness
stages.why: Mermaid source vs its embedded copies. Text comparison, no rendering, which is what lets a zero-dependency repository enforce diagram freshness at all.

stages.name: Decision records
stages.why: Re-derives every recorded number in examples/ledger from its inputs and re-evaluates the decision rule. This is the check the whole pack exists to make mechanical, so it runs before the unit tests: a broken worked example should fail with its own report, not as a test name.

stages.name: Test
stages.why: The unit and contract suite (node:test, no runner dependency).

stages.name: Audit this repository
stages.why: The standards repository is audited by its own audit. Deliberately not --strict: that flag fails on warnings too, which turns every advisory finding into a broken build, and the predictable result is that someone disables the step. The gate on errors is the assertion in test/audit.test.mjs that this repository has no error-severity findings, which ran above.

stages.name: Validate this repository
stages.why: The gate. validate applies this repository's own policy and exits 1 on a required-rule failure or a forbidden-rule violation (BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT), and 2 if a policy cannot be read. This is the command adopting projects are told to gate on, so it is the one this repository gates on.

services.$comment: This repository has no runtime services. docs/architecture.md: 'There is no server, no database, and no network I/O.' The CI container therefore runs with no network at all (compose.ci.yml sets network_mode: none), which turns that architectural claim into an enforced property rather than a statement. A repository reusing this pattern declares its dependencies in compose.ci.yml with healthchecks, and scripts/ci.* will wait on them; see docs/local-ci.md.
